subject: Route callchain reconciliation — cost & latency mapping
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Route callchain reconciliation — cost & latency mapping

Hi team,

Putting this in your inbox to align on a small-but-critical console/observability ask that keeps coming up in customer conversations. TL;DR: customers want a single view that ties per-route cost back to the full callchain (routing -> model variant -> cache hit -> fallback) so they can explain sudden token spend spikes while also understanding tail latency contributors.

Can we scope a minimal MVP that: 
- Surfaces a per-route callchain breakdown (sequence of hops with time & token cost per hop)
- Links each hop to the model variant and node pool that served it
- Flags when fallback routing or cold KV-cache misses contributed > X% of the token cost for the request

Why now: two enterprise deals in procurement asked for this to avoid surprise overages and to support their SRE teams' chargebacks. It's also a recurring ask in CS escalations.

I'd like a short triage: what data do we need that currently isn't emitted, what existing stores can we tie into (trace logs, cost ledger), and a rough engineering estimate (S, M, L). If we can get a quick mockup in Console with an example trace and toggle for cost attribution, that would be ideal for demoing next week.

Questions to help scope:
- Jonas: can our tracing pipeline link token counts to trace spans today?
- Kimberly: how painful is it to export per-hop model variant and pool metadata?
- Ben: will this change any billing pipelines?

I've attached a small synthetic trace to illustrate (sample_route_trace.json) and a screenshot mock (callchain_screenshot.png).

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Console & Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Route callchain reconciliation — cost & latency mapping

On Thu, Apr 11, 2028 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com> wrote:
> Putting this in your inbox to align on a small-but-critical console/observability ask that keeps coming up in customer conversations. TL;DR: customers want a single view that ties per-route cost back to the full callchain (routing -> model variant -> cache hit -> fallback) so they can explain sudden token spend spikes while also understanding tail latency contributors.

+1 on the ask. Quick answers:
- Tracing: our current distributed tracing captures spans for gateway routing and the model-serving hop, but span payloads do not include token counts or quantization/precision metadata. We can add token metadata to the model-serving span; cost ledger joins would then be possible but will need a consistent request_id propagated across components.
- Linking to node pool: we emit node pool id at runtime, but it's not part of the trace index (only logs). We'd need an enrichment job to join traces to node inventory for the UI.
- Fallbacks & cache: we currently tag a span when a fallback occurs, and we emit cache hit/miss as metrics; however cache misses are aggregated, not per-request.

Proposed minimal scope (MVP):
1) Expand model-serving span to include: token_input_count, token_output_count, model_variant, quantization_profile
2) Propagate request_id end-to-end and index it in trace storage
3) Add a lightweight enrichment pipeline that annotates trace spans with node_pool_id (from logs)
4) UI: per-request callchain viewer that shows latency + token counts + cost attribution per hop (toggle between absolute and % share)

Rough effort: 2 weeks infra work (spans + request_id), 1 week enrichment job, 2 weeks UI/console. Assuming parallelization: 5-6 sprint-days from infra + 6-8 sprint-days frontend.

Risks: billing joins must be careful — we cannot retroactively change cost allocations without clear customer comms. Also storage cost for enriched traces could grow; we'll need sampling/retention policies.

If you want, I'll scope an OBS ticket with acceptance criteria and a sample event schema.

— Jonas
Senior Observability Engineer

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Route callchain reconciliation — cost & latency mapping

Thanks for the clear breakdown, Jonas — that aligns with my read. A couple additions from SRE/ops perspective:

- Data retention & sampling: we should only enrich traces for requests that cross a cost/latency threshold to avoid blowup (configurable sampling). Suggest default: enrich when request token cost > $0.05 or tail latency > 1s.
- Backfill/compatibility: for customers who request historical reconciliation, we must surface: "data not available before X date" unless we run an expensive backfill. We'll need product to decide whether backfill is an enterprise-paid service.
- Attachments: I dropped a tiny sample (sample_route_trace.json) that shows three hops (gateway -> model_variant-A -> fallback-model-B) including when cache misses occurred. Also attached a quick mock screenshot.

Operational constraints:
1) Enrichment job can run as a streaming join for live traces; a batch backfill job would be an offline ETL that could take hours for large windows.
2) Billing: Ben — the UI should default to a read-only cost attribution (informational) and not change billing line items until finance signs off. We can show cost breakdown per hop but prefix with "estimated"; any formal chargeback needs a separate alignment.

If product wants a short PO (scope + data retention + "backfill paid option"), I can write it up and attach estimated infra cost.

Kimberly
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Route callchain reconciliation — cost & latency mapping

Thanks — this makes sense. A few quick notes from billing/ops side:
- Agree with the "estimated" prefix. We should avoid any UI that suggests a finalized invoice-level cost unless finance is in the loop.
- For enterprise customers requesting backfills as part of contract negotiations, we can price a one-time backfill. I'll coordinate with finance to draft a standard quote template.
- Please tag the OBS ticket with the prospective account if the customer asked; that helps prioritize.

Looping in internal stakeholder: marissa — happy to own the pricing side if you want a table for AMs.

— Ben
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
